newsitem.title: USA: Deaf Mexicans claim they were "slaves" in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Deaf Mexicans claim they were "slaves" in U.S..

text.p: Dozens of deaf Mexicans, many claiming in sign language they were forced to work for slave wages in the United States, were rescued on Saturday after four of them reported their plight to police.

The four walked into the 115th police precinct in Jackson Heights section in the New York City borough of Queens at 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT) with a bizarre story that their compatriots were being held captive at two separate locations. It was not clear how the four men got away, police said.
Police said the two locations were not far from the station precinct.
Of the 62 people at the two houses, 10 were children, ranging in age from a three week-old infant to nine years old.
"Some of the children seemed to be in good health," the spokesman said. "The children only speak Spanish," police spokesman Arek Tarih said.

"They were all deaf mutes but one of the Mexicans was able to communicate with us that he was brought here from Mexico and that he works in the street selling pens and toys and that the money he makes goes to the boss who brought him to the States from Mexico," Tarih said.
"He said he works for very little or no money at all," police quoted the man as saying.
"We are still trying to sort out what transpired. It is not clear where in Mexico these people were recruited and who brought them here," the spokesman said.

Police are communicating with the deaf mutes through translators and sign language interpreters. "They are telling us they are legal immigrants but that their documents were taken away from them by the person who brought them to the United States," Tarih said.
He said those claims have not been verified and were under investigation.
Forty-four people were found at the first location and 18 others at the second site. They were all taken by bus to the police precinct.
Police said the Red Cross was assisting in feeding and finding housing for the Mexicans.
